title: The UK half is an investment case, not a recovery case: 52% of /uk/ pages have never earned a single impression in 16 months

evidence.claim: All-country traffic to /uk/ paths over the full 16-month window is 15,741 impressions and 253 clicks across 156 distinct pages
326 /uk/ pages return 200 (crawl), so 170 of 326 (52%) have never earned one impression in 16 months
GB is the second-largest market by impressions but only 12.7% of GB impressions land on /uk/ pages
evidence.value: GB total 67,857 impressions; /uk/ paths 8,627 (12.7%); US paths 59,230 (87.3%)

evidence.claim: Ahrefs sees almost no GB organic footprint: 10 ranked GB keywords for the whole domain, of which /uk/ pages hold 3
evidence.value: top GB keywords: 'it outsourcing' vol 800 pos 1 (US path); 'typescript developer' vol 40 pos 10 (/uk path); 'cloud employee' vol 30 pos 1 (/uk)

evidence.claim: GB /uk/ pages rank materially worse than the US pages GB searchers actually see
evidence.value: /uk/ paths wpos 31.6 vs US paths wpos 22.6 for GB searchers

impact.estimate: Framing finding: there is nothing to 'recover'; localisation is a bet on winning GB demand currently going to US pages (59,230 GB impressions on US paths, 149 clicks)

recommendation: Treat D1 as investment, sized against the 67,857 GB impressions/16mo actually observed (about 4,200/month). Do not promise a recovery; the /uk/ pages never had rankings to lose.

title: The apparent /uk/ CTR advantage is an artefact: 242 of 245 GB /uk/ clicks come from the /uk homepage on brand queries; the other 123 /uk/ pages earned 3 clicks total

evidence.claim: GB /uk/ paths show 8,627 impressions / 245 clicks (2.84% CTR) vs GB US-paths 0.25% CTR - an 11x gap that does not survive decomposition
Excluding the /uk homepage, GB /uk/ pages earned 3 clicks on 6,733 impressions in 16 months
Ahrefs confirms the /uk homepage traffic is brand: its only ranked GB keyword is 'cloud employee' (vol 30, pos 1)

impact.estimate: Prevents a false conclusion at synthesis: /uk/ pages do NOT outperform - non-brand /uk/ CTR is 0.04% on 6,733 impressions

recommendation: Any lens or synthesis reading that says 'UK pages convert better' must be discarded. The clone pages convert essentially nothing; that is the strongest data argument FOR real differentiation and better titles.

title: DFH-2 answered: one shared Sanity document serves both locales; zero locale='uk' documents exist in production, so Seb cannot edit UK copy independently today

evidence.claim: The production dataset holds zero documents with locale='uk'; 290 documents carry locale='default'
evidence.source: Live GROQ against Sanity project lzbhll1u dataset production: {uk: count(*[locale=="uk"]), default: count(*[locale=="default"]), all: count(*[])}

evidence.claim: A localeField() ('Default (US)' | 'UK') exists in the schema and is applied to 13 document types, but is a dormant migration artefact - no query filters detail content on it
evidence.source: studio/schemas/_shared.ts lines 7-28; grep localeField() across studio/schemas (13 hits)
evidence.value: field exists, unused for routing content

evidence.claim: UK routes fetch the identical document by slug; the only locale-aware GROQ predicate is VISIBLE_IN_LOCALE, which gates the single ukOnly document (Caitlin Murray), not content variants
evidence.source: site/src/lib/sanity/queries/_filters.ts line 40; site/src/app/uk/technology/[slug]/page.tsx (fetchTechnology(slug) with no locale param)

impact.estimate: Blocking: no UK copy of any kind (body OR metadata) can be authored until this is decided and wired. Everything else in this lens depends on it

recommendation: Decide the architecture before any content work. Recommendation: locale-override fields on the shared document (ukMetaTitle/ukMetaDescription plus an optional ukBody/uk section overrides), NOT separate documents. Separate docs would fork 326 documents, duplicate every reference, break the single-slug hreflang pairing (UK-07), and contradict the existing single-doc route architecture. Override fields keep slugs paired, let Seb edit UK copy in the same Studio form, and degrade gracefully (missing override = current behaviour). Estimated wiring: 2-3 days of schema + query + template work by Claude.

title: Site-wide metadata duplication IS the UK problem: 305 of 306 duplicate-title groups and 321 of 322 duplicate-description groups are pure UK/US pairs

evidence.claim: 305 of 306 duplicate-title groups reduce to exactly {path, /uk+path} once query-string variants are normalised
evidence.source: crawl/duplicate-titles.json (306 groups), pair-normalisation script this session

evidence.claim: 321 of 322 duplicate-description groups are likewise pure UK/US pairs
Every one of the 307 word-identical UK pairs also has identical title AND identical description

impact.estimate: A UK-metadata pass across all 326 clears ~99% of site-wide metadata duplication in one move and gives the 6,733 zero-click GB impressions (UK-02) a British snippet to click. At even 1% CTR that is ~4 clicks/month; the larger prize is GB queries currently resolving to US pages (59,230 impressions). Estimate, low confidence

recommendation: Do the metadata pass across ALL 326 pages FIRST, before body-content work on the 10. It is cheap once UK-03's override fields exist (templated first draft: £-currency, UK phrasing, 'UK' geo-qualifier where the query data supports it; Seb reviews). Not a formal quick win only because it depends on the UK-03 schema decision.

title: The 19 already-differing UK pages are accidents, not localisation - the 'natural experiment' is void and shows no performance benefit

evidence.claim: Verdict split is 307 identical / 18 differing / 1 no-US-counterpart (the known ukOnly Caitlin Murray page, Tech Debt #58)
10 of the 18 differ ONLY in title with body jaccard >= 0.86 and equal word counts (e.g. 3 technology pages and 6 team pages at jaccard 1.0 or ~0.9); none of these is a deliberate UK variant

The two big body divergences are known artefacts: /uk/compare/cloud-employee-vs-arc-dev (jaccard 0.269) is the US-side accidental redirect shadow (Tech Debt #55); /uk/tools/price-comparison-calculator (jaccard 0.451) is a client-rendered calculator the word-count method cannot see evenly
The differing pages perform no better in GB: /uk/technology/azure-developers 102 impressions, 0 clicks, position 60.9; qase and unity-developers earn no recorded GB impressions

impact.estimate: No evidence either way on whether differentiation lifts rankings - the sample is accidental and earns ~nothing. The D1 bet remains unproven by internal data

recommendation: Do not cite these 18 as evidence for or against localisation. Treat Phase A itself as the experiment: localise 10, hold the rest as controls, read GB positions at +60 and +90 days.

title: The Phase A ten, ranked on 16 months of GB demand: toptal-vs-upwork, home, nodejs, philippines-developers, typescript, python, aws, how-it-works, about-us/contact, pricing

evidence.claim: GB impressions per logical page (US+UK path combined, commercial templates only, 16 months): /compare/toptal-vs-upwork 4,694 (pos 9.4, 0 clicks); / 4,031 (329 clicks, brand); /technology/nodejs-developers 2,412; /services/philippines-developers 2,087; /technology/typescript-developers 1,983 (pos 11.5); /technology/python-developers 1,424; /technology/aws-developers 1,346; /about-us 1,036 (pos 6.1); /technology/openai-developers 689; /contact 582 (pos 6.0); /how-it-works 495 (pos 7.7)
evidence.source: gsc/full-page-x-country.json, country=gbr, /uk prefix folded onto US path

evidence.claim: /uk/technology/typescript-developers already ranks pos 6.9 on 396 GB impressions with 0 clicks, and holds the domain's only non-brand /uk/ Ahrefs GB keyword ('typescript developer', vol 40, pos 10)
/pricing shows negligible recorded GB impressions but is the D1 currency page par excellence (£ vs $); its inclusion is judgment, not data, and is labelled as such
evidence.source: gsc/full-page-x-country.json (no /pricing row in GB top set)

impact.estimate: The ten cover 18,600 of the 67,857 GB impressions (27%). toptal-vs-upwork alone: 4,694 impressions at position 9.4 with 0 clicks; a UK-differentiated page holding position 5-6 at 2% CTR would be roughly 6-8 clicks/month from that page. Whole set: plausibly 20-40 GB clicks/month at +90 days. Estimate, low confidence - GB volumes are small

recommendation: Phase A order: (1) typescript-developers - already page 1 in GB, cheapest test; (2) toptal-vs-upwork - largest GB demand, position 9.4; (3) philippines-developers; (4) nodejs; (5) python; (6) aws; (7) how-it-works; (8) home; (9) about-us + contact (UK contact details, low writing cost); (10) pricing (currency). Roughly 3-4h of Seb copy per page plus review; lead data cannot inform this ranking (leads_* null throughout, per manifest) - it is ranked on traffic and stated as such.

title: hreflang is clean on all real pages today - the localisation programme has three specific ways to break it, all avoidable

evidence.claim: 656 crawled pages carry hreflang; only 9 rows have reciprocity issues and every one is a query-string URL variant (?ref=, ?page=), not a real page
evidence.source: crawl/hreflang.json (656 rows, 9 with issues, all containing '?')

evidence.claim: hreflang pairing is generated from the shared slug (generateHreflang(usPath)), so it survives only while UK and US URLs stay slug-paired

impact.estimate: Protective: losing reciprocal hreflang on 326 pairs would re-expose 307 word-identical pages as raw duplicates

recommendation: Three rules for the programme: (1) never fork UK pages onto different slugs (rules out the separate-documents answer to UK-03 unless slugs are pinned); (2) if any never-earning UK pages are pruned (UK-08), remove BOTH the page and the US side's en-GB hreflang pointer in the same change, or Google sees a dangling pointer; (3) keep canonicals self-referencing on UK pages - a 'canonical to US' shortcut would deindex the UK half wholesale and silently undo D1.

title: Phase B should be a triage, not a 316-page rewrite: 170 UK pages have earned zero impressions in 16 months and most should stay as hreflang'd clones indefinitely

evidence.claim: 170 of 326 /uk/ pages: zero impressions, any country, 16 months
Of the 156 that have earned impressions, 124 earned them from GB; the GB tail below the top ~30 pages is under 100 impressions each over 16 months
There is no duplicate-content penalty to escape: hreflang is correctly implemented (UK-07), so a clone that earns nothing costs nothing beyond crawl budget

impact.estimate: Avoids ~450+ hours of copywriting (316 pages x ~1.5h minimum) that the demand data cannot justify; concentrates Seb's hours on the ~40-50 pages with any recorded GB demand

recommendation: Phase B = metadata-localise everything (UK-04), then body-localise only pages that clear a demand bar (>=100 GB impressions/16mo or a ranked GB keyword): roughly 30-50 pages, ~150h. The remaining ~270 stay as clones with UK metadata; revisit quarterly against fresh GSC. This is a deliberate narrowing of D1's 'every remaining UK page gets worked through' - flagged for Jake to ratify, since D1 is his locked decision.
